title: SDK background context fence and non-blocking span handoff
creator: Anika Patel
description: Add a lightweight SDK feature to ensure reliable tracing context propagation for background tasks and async workers across languages. Many services drop spans when work is handed to background threads, worker pools, or message handlers (async callbacks, goroutines, node worker threads, Celery/RQ tasks). This ticket implements a 'context fence' and a non-blocking span handoff queue inside the SDK to: 1) capture and attach a minimal provenance envelope before task dispatch, 2) enqueue a deferred span attachment that resumes/links the span in the target worker without blocking the request path, 3) suppress high-cardinality tags on background spans by default, and 4) provide opt-in APIs for explicit context transfer. The goal is <1% p50 request latency overhead for synchronous paths and reliable end-to-end trace stitching for background processing. Languages in scope: Python (asyncio + Celery), Node (async hooks + worker threads), Go (goroutines), Java (executor threadpools).
acceptance_criteria: E2E traces show a single trace id across request -> background task -> downstream service for representative workloads in each supported language
Instrumented SDK adds <1% p50 latency on hot path for a simple echo endpoint with tracing enabled (benchmarks attached)
Background spans default to suppressed high-cardinality tags (no customer IDs in attributes) unless opt-in flag enabled
Feature can be toggled via SDK config and rollout percentage in console. No binary-breaking changes to existing SDK surface
Automated integration tests cover context capture, deferred handoff, and failure retry semantics
comments: 2026-02-20 - Triage: PM flagged multiple customer incidents where background tasks were missing from traces. Scope agreed for SDK-level mitigation rather than infra-only fix.

2026-02-24 - Design sync: Decided on an async handoff queue inside SDK that writes a small provenance blob into in-memory queue and optionally into durable queue (for serverless lifecycles). Chose non-blocking over synchronous propagation to keep request latency predictable.

2026-02-28 - Benchmarking: prototype in Python (asyncio) shows 0.6% p50 overhead with local in-memory queue, 1.5% with durable queue (disk-backed). Plan to default to in-memory with durable as opt-in for long-running processes.
2026-03-03 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/782 - implements context fence and background worker decorator. Needs engineering review for thread-safety.

2026-03-06 - Review notes from infra: confirm sampling alignment with edge sampler and ensure no double-sampling when background task re-injects span. Also need tests for partial failures where worker dies before ack.
2026-03-10 - Implementation: core queue + linker done for Python and Go. Node prototype pending async_hooks adjustments. Added console feature flag hook for rollout control.
Follow-ups: create integration harness to run cross-language scenarios in k8s e2e cluster, schedule load tests at scale, and create observability dashboard to validate rollout metrics.
test_plan: Unit tests for fence capture and queue, integration tests that spin up a mock worker to assert trace linkage, language matrix e2e job that runs traces across Python/Node/Go/Java, performance benchmarks comparing baseline vs feature on representative workloads, and chaos test that kills worker mid-processing to assert no resource leaks and proper span status.
implementation_notes: Context envelope must be <512 bytes to avoid queue/backlog amplification
Use ring-buffer for in-process queue with lock-free append where supported (Java Disruptor-style, Go channels), fallback to mutex-protected queue if needed
Default behavior: capture trace id + parent span id + sampling decision + minimal tags (service, route). High-card tags stripped unless explicit transfer flag set
Provide debug-mode verbose provenance that can be enabled per-service for debugging without releasing to customers
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: queue growth in bursty workloads could OOM. Mitigation: bounded ring-buffer with drop-policy and metrics for dropped envelopes; fallback durable write option for long-tail jobs
Risk: inconsistent sampling between caller and worker. Mitigation: carry sampling decision in envelope and honor it on worker; add reconciler job to adjust mismatches in telemetry
Risk: added complexity could regress existing SDKs. Mitigation: incremental rollout, feature flag, language-specific integration tests, and clear deprecation path if needed
